findings.title: Star Blizzard refines phishing and malware delivery with the RedFlick technique
findings.summary_md: Microsoft Threat Intelligence's primary advisory names the RedFlick delivery technique, which uses scheduled tasks to deploy the CosmicPulse Python backdoor after a single user interaction with a password-protected archive. It counts at least 13 large-scale campaigns from January to August 2026 affecting over 100 organizations, primarily in the United States and United Kingdom. The post provides detections, hunting queries, and IoCs, including C2 IP 103.245.213[.]217, the registry key HKCU\Software\Classes\.mollis, and scheduled task names Internet Quality Test Connection, Network Configuration Manager, and System Health Monitor.

findings.title: Spearphishing via Fake URC 2026 Invitations Targets Ukrainian CSOs
findings.summary_md: Digital Security Lab Ukraine documented a spearphishing campaign active from June 10, 2026 that impersonated politician Pawel Kowal and the Ukraine Recovery Conference to target Ukrainian civil society. The chain used a reply-gated password-protected ZIP containing a Files.vhdx disk image, an LNK with its script hidden in the Description field, and four scheduled tasks including SecureDNSObserver, with WebDAV delivery from 89[.]125[.]66[.]183 and remote command sources 103[.]160[.]59[.]97 and secure-dns-hub[.]com. These techniques and IoCs overlap with what Microsoft later folded into its RedFlick reporting, making this the earliest public documentation of the chain.

findings.title: Russian APT Star Blizzard Adopts DarkSword iOS Exploit Kit
findings.summary_md: Proofpoint attributed a March 26, 2026 email campaign using Atlantic Council lures to Star Blizzard, marking the first time the group was observed targeting iCloud accounts and Apple devices. Messages sent from compromised sender addresses redirected iPhone browsers to the DarkSword exploit kit, which had leaked on GitHub, for credential harvesting and intelligence collection. Proofpoint also noted a significant increase in malicious email volume over the preceding two weeks.

findings.title: Russia-Linked APT Star Blizzard Uses ClickFix to Deploy New LostKeys Malware, Google Warns
findings.summary_md: Google reported that Star Blizzard used fake CAPTCHA pages and the ClickFix technique to deliver a new malware family named LostKeys in campaigns observed in January, March, and April 2025 against advisors to Western governments, journalists, think tanks, and NGOs. LostKeys steals files from a hard-coded list of extensions and directories and was deployed only in highly selective cases. This documents the multi-step malware delivery tradecraft that RedFlick later replaced.

findings.title: CISA Issues Warning for Russian 'Star Blizzard' APT Spear-Phishing Operation
findings.summary_md: CISA and partner agencies issued joint advisory AA23-341A attributing Star Blizzard to Russia's FSB Centre 18 and warning of spear-phishing against academia, defense, government, NGOs, and think tanks in the US, UK, NATO countries, and states neighboring Russia. The advisory described methodical research and rapport-building before credential theft, often to victims' personal email addresses to bypass corporate controls. It also noted 2022 expansion into defense-industrial targets and US Department of Energy facilities.
